_comment: The ConPTY that ships beside the executable, pinned by hash.
Windows' own in-box ConPTY is still the v1 design on every build we have
measured (including 10.0.26200): it parses the child's VT into a text
buffer and re-renders a snapshot into our pipe. That drops whole
sequences (APC, DCS), rewrites others (OSC 8 loses its parameters and its
terminator), reorders OSC against the text around it, and -- measured on
this project's own stack -- spends 286ms and 2.93MB where the v2
redistributable spends 119ms and 2.17MB for the same 10,000 lines of
Japanese, measured on this project's own stack.
tools/conpty.ps1 downloads this package, checks every hash below, and
puts conpty.dll and OpenConsole.exe into vendor/conpty/. dist.list is what
then carries them to the exe. portable-pty loads a conpty.dll sitting
beside the executable in preference to the in-box one with no help from
us, so there is no Rust code behind this -- only the file being there.
Both files are Microsoft's, signed by Microsoft, and MIT-licensed. We
never re-sign them. To raise the version: change every field here, run
tools/conpty.ps1 -Force, and check the new hashes are what came down.
